data.content_ref: inline:The target claims the distinction between independent and correlated failures is 'uniquely evidenced' by temporal signature/Poisson distribution, but its own first countercondition refutes this uniqueness: a slow-burn shared cause (e.g., memory leak triggered by local load) produces staggered failures that do NOT cluster tightly around a singular t-zero event and can mimic a Poisson process. The problem asks for evidence that would distinguish failures that 'merely appear uncorrelated until a shared cause is found'; a slow-burn shared cause is precisely such a case, and the target's temporal-signature mechanism cannot detect it because the variance in failure start-times will not be tight around any known external event. So the claimed unique evidentiary value of the temporal signature fails against the very countercondition the target admits.
